fichas.title: Sustainable Building: Operation and Demolition
fichas.summary: Sustainability depends on the relationship of a design to its location and purpose, usable and effective structures, durability, material ageing characteristics, flexibility of use, and potential for conversion. Because buildings have long useful lives, operation is a significant phase of their life cycle. Design and regular updating should support energy-saving operation, resource conservation, reuse of water and energy, health, thermal comfort, and lower operating, maintenance, and cleaning costs.

fichas.title: Potential Savings of Heating and Electrical Energy
fichas.summary: The page lists measures for reducing energy use in heating, domestic hot water, lighting, heating and cooling, air conditioning, and electrical devices. Measures include room-level temperature and time controls, regulation circuits for differing requirements, daylight use, efficient lamps and equipment, reduced air flows and cooling loads, and switching devices off at the mains when feasible.

fichas.title: Ecological, Economic, and Technical Criteria for Waste Disposal
fichas.summary: The waste-disposal evaluation considers ecological impacts such as transport, emissions, land use, materials, and disposal energy; economic criteria such as regulations, recycling acceptance, capacity, and costs; and technical criteria such as high-quality recycling and feasibility. It also considers the environmental effects of material production and thermal exploitation of building waste.

fichas.title: Disposal Routes: Basics of Recycling
fichas.summary: The disposal hierarchy shown proceeds through avoidance, including reuse and further use of components; exploitation, including recycling, downcycling, and thermal exploitation; and disposal, including composting and landfill.

fichas.title: Application of Cycles in a Residential Building
fichas.summary: A diagram of a residential building in Freiburg-Vauban illustrates resource cycles involving solar gain, photovoltaics, solar collectors, rainwater, greywater and foul water, kitchen waste, cooking gas, fertilizer or compost, biogas, and combined heat and power. The drawing labels a sand filter and routes for water, energy, and waste.
